verdicts.reasoning: Verified the KICKOFF text verbatim at devkit-pipeline/KICKOFF.md lines 155-162 and the SKILL.md sentences it echoes. The prompt restates the skill's own frontmatter trigger description almost clause-for-clause ('surface what must be true' / 'surface hidden assumptions'; 'scored importance x evidence' / 'score them by importance and evidence'; 'cheapest experiment for the top few' / 'cheapest experiments to test the riskiest ones first'), and also re-lists the VUBF category names the skill dedicates a whole section to (lines 19-43) plus the numbered extraction-process steps (scoring, ranking top 3-5, suggesting cheapest experiment, lines 70-73). This is the skill's own internal methodology and taxonomy re-derived in the operator prompt, not an invocation parameter the skill can't already know -- squarely redundant-restatement. Medium severity because it duplicates a non-trivial chunk of methodology (taxonomy + scoring axis + ranking step), not just a one-word emphasis.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by reading the full SKILL.md: it defines assumption extraction, scoring, ranking, and experiment suggestions, and stops there -- it never assigns execution responsibility. The KICKOFF clause 'the skill stops at experiment design, and most VUBF tests (fake-door, landing page, interviews) are mine to execute, not yours' is a human/agent task-division instruction the skill has no way to encode about itself (it can't know who is invoking it or what the operator will do with its output). This is load-bearing operator context, not restated methodology, even though the boundary it draws happens to coincide with where the skill's own scope already ends.
